display.purpose: The 'Almanac' wordmark and finale titles. Extreme 0.55em tracking is the signature; the word spreads across the header like stars across a horizon.

headline.purpose: The category-select prompt ('Which sky will you chart?') and the finale tier name.

question.purpose: The live trivia question, set large and light in Outfit with a faint ember text-glow. Drops to 24px under 720px.

body.purpose: Supporting copy and answer text. Prose capped at 65-75ch; the finale toast uses a 46ch measure.

label.purpose: The meta row ('Star 03 / 10'), category captions, verdict lines. Small, wide, quiet.

shadows.name: ember-hover-tile
shadows.purpose: Hover/focus glow on category tiles. Signals energy, never height.

shadows.name: ember-hover-answer
shadows.purpose: Hover/focus glow on answer rows, tighter than the tile glow.

shadows.name: star-glow
shadows.purpose: On lit star-chart nodes and the current-question pulse.

shadows.name: score-glow
shadows.purpose: The big finale score numeral only.

motion.name: ease-star
motion.purpose: The only easing in the system. Every entrance settles without overshoot; no bounce, no elastic.

motion.name: aurora-move
motion.purpose: Slow translate-only drift on the blurred aurora blobs. Transform-only keeps them on the compositor.

motion.name: star-pulse
motion.purpose: Opacity pulse on the current-question node in the star chart.

motion.name: drift-in
motion.purpose: Staggered entrance for category tiles and answer rows (60ms step).

motion.name: orbit-spin
motion.purpose: The loader's ember satellite circling its gold core.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The main action, used to advance a question or replay. Ember text on a whisper-thin ember wash.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; border-radius: 9999px; padding: 16px 36px; font-family: Unbounded, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 300; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.34em; cursor: pointer; color: var(--color-ember, #ffb38a); background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-ember, #ffb38a) 5%, transparent); border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-ember, #ffb38a) 50%, transparent); transition: background 300ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), box-shadow 300ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-ember, #ffb38a) 15%, transparent); box-shadow: 0 0 30px -4px var(--color-ember, #ffb38a); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--color-ember, #ffb38a); }

components.name: Quiet Button
components.description: The secondary finale action. Transparent with a fog border; hover lifts the text to starlight.
components.css: .ds-btn-quiet { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; border-radius: 9999px; padding: 16px 36px; font-family: Unbounded, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 300; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.34em; cursor: pointer; background: transparent; color: var(--color-fog, #aab3cd); border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-fog, #aab3cd) 40%, transparent); transition: color 300ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), border-color 300ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-btn-quiet:hover { color: var(--color-starlight, #e8eeff); border-color: var(--color-fog, #aab3cd); } .ds-btn-quiet:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--color-ember, #ffb38a); }

components.name: Category Tile
components.description: One of four glass tiles on the opening screen. Monochrome ember icon in a disc, wide-tracked caption, 3px lift on hover.
components.css: .ds-tile { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 12px; padding: 24px 16px; border-radius: 12px; cursor: pointer; background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-starlight, #e8eeff) 3%, transparent); border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-starlight, #e8eeff) 12%, transparent); backdrop-filter: blur(4px); transition: transform 300ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), border-color 300ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), background 300ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), box-shadow 300ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-tile:hover { transform: translateY(-3px); border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-ember, #ffb38a) 60%, transparent); background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-ember, #ffb38a) 5%, transparent); box-shadow: 0 0 40px -8px var(--color-ember, #ffb38a); } .ds-tile:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--color-ember, #ffb38a); } .ds-tile-icon { display: grid; place-content: center; width: 46px; height: 46px; color: var(--color-ember, #ffb38a); } .ds-tile-name { font-family: Unbounded, sans-serif; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 300; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.12em; color: var(--color-starlight, #e8eeff); } .ds-tile-meta { font-size: 9.5px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.3em; color: var(--color-fog, #aab3cd); }

components.name: Answer Row
components.description: A glass label wrapping a real radio. All four share a name, so the group keeps native arrow-key movement and a single tab stop.
components.css: .ds-answer { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 14px; padding: 14px 22px; border-radius: 12px; cursor: pointer; font-family: Outfit, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 300; line-height: 24px; color: var(--color-starlight, #e8eeff); background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-starlight, #e8eeff) 3%, transparent); border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-starlight, #e8eeff) 15%, transparent); backdrop-filter: blur(4px); transition: border-color 200ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), background 200ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), box-shadow 200ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-answer:hover { border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-ember, #ffb38a) 60%, transparent); background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-ember, #ffb38a) 5%, transparent); box-shadow: 0 0 26px -6px var(--color-ember, #ffb38a); } .ds-answer:has(:focus-visible) { box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--color-ember, #ffb38a); } .ds-answer-dot { appearance: none; margin: 0; width: 10px; height: 10px; flex: none; border-radius: 9999px; outline: none; cursor: pointer; background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-starlight, #e8eeff) 25%, transparent); transition: background 200ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-answer-dot:checked { background: var(--color-ember, #ffb38a); box-shadow: 0 0 10px var(--color-ember, #ffb38a); }

components.name: Answer Row (locked correct)
components.description: The resolved correct choice. Green border and tint with a glowing green dot; green now reads as complementary against the red sky.
components.css: .ds-answer-correct { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 14px; padding: 14px 22px; border-radius: 12px; font-family: Outfit, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 300; line-height: 24px; color: var(--color-starlight, #e8eeff); background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-correct, #7be8a2) 8%, transparent); border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-correct, #7be8a2) 70%, transparent); backdrop-filter: blur(4px); } .ds-dot-correct { width: 10px; height: 10px; flex: none; border-radius: 9999px; background: var(--color-correct, #7be8a2); box-shadow: 0 0 10px var(--color-correct, #7be8a2); }

components.name: Answer Row (locked wrong)
components.description: The chosen wrong answer. Signal Rose is held 21 degrees off the backdrop hue so the error still reads as an alarm rather than atmosphere.
components.css: .ds-answer-wrong { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 14px; padding: 14px 22px; border-radius: 12px; font-family: Outfit, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 300; line-height: 24px; color: var(--color-starlight, #e8eeff); background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-wrong, #ffa8cf) 8%, transparent); border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-wrong, #ffa8cf) 70%, transparent); backdrop-filter: blur(4px); } .ds-dot-wrong { width: 10px; height: 10px; flex: none; border-radius: 9999px; background: var(--color-wrong, #ffa8cf); box-shadow: 0 0 10px var(--color-wrong, #ffa8cf); }

components.name: Star Chart Progress
components.description: The signature component. Ten nodes across the top of the play area: gold and glowing when correct, fog when missed, pulsing ember for the current question, dim for the ones ahead. Lines light gold between adjacent answered nodes.
components.css: .ds-chart { width: 100%; } .ds-chart svg { width: 100%; height: 64px; overflow: visible; } .ds-chart-line { stroke: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-fog, #aab3cd) 40%, transparent); stroke-width: 1; } .ds-chart-line-lit { stroke: var(--color-stargold, #ffd98e); stroke-width: 1; opacity: 0.7; } .ds-node-gold { fill: var(--color-stargold, #ffd98e); filter: drop-shadow(0 0 6px var(--color-stargold, #ffd98e)); } .ds-node-current { fill: var(--color-ember, #ffb38a); filter: drop-shadow(0 0 6px var(--color-ember, #ffb38a)); animation: ds-pulse 1.4s cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1) infinite; } .ds-node-future { fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-starlight, #e8eeff) 20%, transparent); } @keyframes ds-pulse { 0%, 100% { opacity: 1; } 50% { opacity: 0.35; } }

components.name: Loader
components.description: Shown while the model generates a round. A gold core with a dashed ring and one ember satellite in orbit; a spinner rather than a skeleton because the wait has unknowable shape.
components.html: Charting the sky…
components.css: .ds-loader { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; gap: 28px; padding: 64px 0; text-align: center; } .ds-loader-orbit { position: relative; width: 90px; height: 90px; } .ds-loader-core { position: absolute; inset: 34px; border-radius: 9999px; background: var(--color-stargold, #ffd98e); box-shadow: 0 0 24px var(--color-stargold, #ffd98e); } .ds-loader-ring { position: absolute; inset: 0; border-radius: 9999px; border: 1px dashed color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-starlight, #e8eeff) 20%, transparent); animation: ds-orbit 3s linear infinite; } .ds-loader-sat { position: absolute; top: -5px; left: 50%; width: 10px; height: 10px; border-radius: 9999px; background: var(--color-ember, #ffb38a); box-shadow: 0 0 10px var(--color-ember, #ffb38a); } .ds-loader-caption { font-family: Unbounded, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 300; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.34em; color: var(--color-fog, #aab3cd); } @keyframes ds-orbit { to { rotate: 360deg; } }

narrative.overview:
This is the hour before dawn at a high-altitude observatory: the dome is open, a red aurora is burning low across the sky, and one instrument glows softly in front of you. The interface is atmosphere first and controls second. A near-black canvas holds a bank of deep red washes and a scatter of twinkling stars; the UI sits on top in restrained translucent glass, never a solid slab, never a bright card. The signature idea is that your score is not a readout but a drawing: each answered question lights a star in a chart that assembles itself across the top of the play area, gold for a hit, faded for a miss.

The red is doing real work. An earlier version of this system ran cool teal-green over the same black, which is the reflex palette for anything described as "cosmic" and made the interface read as generic sci-fi. Turning the sky red moved it somewhere specific: aurora australis, a blood moon, an old star atlas printed in rust. Because the backdrop is now warm, the single interactive accent had to move with it, from teal to a soft peach ember. Warm-on-warm reads as one world instead of two competing ones.

The system rejects the visual language of the category on purpose. It is not a quiz-app playground, not a gamified casino, not a corporate dashboard, and not AI slop. Restraint is the point: one accent does the work, the wordmark carries its weight through wide tracking rather than a fill, and the sky does the rest.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black canvas beneath a bank of deep red aurora washes.
Frameless, translucent-glass surfaces; no opaque cards.
One working accent (ember peach); gold is earned, never decorative.
Progress rendered as a self-drawing star chart.
Unbounded display with extreme letter-spacing; airy light-weight Outfit body.
Motion is meaningful and eased-out; every animation names an event.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Ember is the only interactive color. If a control lights up, hovers, focuses, or pulses, it is ember, never gold, violet, or green. Gold cannot be used to signal interactivity; it only marks something already won.

rules.name: The Earned Gold Rule
rules.body: Gold appears only as a consequence of a correct answer or a finished score. It is forbidden as decoration, as a border, or as a hover state.

rules.name: The Hue Distance Rule
rules.body: Because the backdrop is red, any color carrying meaning must sit at least 20 degrees of hue away from it. Measure before shipping a semantic color; a signal that shares the sky's hue is not a signal.

rules.name: The Single Source Rule
rules.body: The canvas washes are mixed from the aurora tokens with color-mix, never restated as literal rgba(). Backdrop and palette move together or they drift.

rules.name: The Wide-Tracking Rule
rules.body: Every uppercase Unbounded label carries at least 0.22em tracking, and the wordmark carries 0.55em. Tight uppercase is forbidden; the spacing is what makes it feel cosmic rather than corporate.

rules.name: The Display-In-Controls Exception
rules.body: Product convention says keep display faces out of buttons and labels. This system overrides that on purpose: the wide-tracked Unbounded label is the brand, and it appears on buttons, meta rows, and captions. The override is deliberate and documented; do not fix it by swapping in a body font.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Surfaces cast no drop shadows. If something needs to feel active, it glows; if it needs separation, it uses translucency and blur. A 2014-style dark box-shadow under a card is forbidden.

rules.name: The Fixed-Layer Rule
rules.body: All atmosphere renders on one position: fixed layer (.aurora-canvas, applied to the NightSky element). background-attachment: fixed is forbidden; it repaints badly on iOS Safari over multi-stop radial gradients.

dos: Do keep ember as the only interactive color and gold as reward-only (the One Voice and Earned Gold rules).
Do measure hue distance and contrast against the deepest aurora overlap on a glass surface, not against flat Void. That is the tightest case; anything that passes there passes everywhere.
Do render foreground surfaces as translucent glass over the live sky (bg-starlight/3, backdrop-blur-sm), so the aurora reads faintly through.
Do convey depth with glow and translucency, never drop shadows (the No-Shadow rule).
Do track uppercase Unbounded labels at 0.22em or wider (the Wide-Tracking rule).
Do mix backdrop colors from the aurora tokens with color-mix (the Single Source rule).
Do map every animation to a real event (a star igniting, the sky charting) and ease out; provide a prefers-reduced-motion settle for all ambient motion.
Do let native form semantics do the work: a shared radio name instead of hand-rolled Tab interception.
Do keep progress available to screen readers via the chart's live-text fallback; never rely on color alone.
donts: Don't reintroduce opaque cards or a white panel; no card grids, and never nest a glass surface inside another.
Don't drift toward generic quiz-app SaaS (Kahoot/Quizizz primary-color cartoon energy, bubbly rounded mascots).
Don't turn it into a gamified neon casino (coin showers, slot glitz, streak-pressure reward loops).
Don't let it flatten into a flat corporate dashboard (Material/Bootstrap gray-on-white card grids, zero atmosphere).
Don't ship AI slop: no gradient text anywhere (the wordmark and finale title are solid color), no decorative glassmorphism on opaque pages, no hero-metric template, no identical card grids.
Don't use a semantic color that shares the backdrop's hue. If it looks like part of the sky, it has stopped being a signal.
Don't use #000 or #fff for surfaces or text; the canvas is Void (#050810) and text is Starlight (#e8eeff).
Don't put a colored border-left stripe on any row or callout; answer states use full borders + tint.
Don't use background-attachment: fixed; atmosphere belongs on the one fixed NightSky layer.
Don't hand-roll keyboard navigation for standard controls. If you are intercepting Tab, you have skipped a native affordance.
